prerequisites: Student knows and understands basic principles of physics, especially electrostatics and electromagnetism.
Student is able to compute differential and integral calculus.
Student defines and solves correctly problems connected with the profession.

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows basic principles of electrical circuits and electromagnetism and their utilization in electrical machines and devices.
Student knows principles, construction and destination of transformers and chokes.
Student knows construction and characteristics of electrical machines.
Student is able to build measurement circuit and make measurements of basic electrical quantities.
Student is able to make simple laboratory measurements of electrical devices.
Student is able to determine of characteristics of basic electrical motors.
Student is aware of their own responsibility for their work and a willingness to comply with the principles of teamwork.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Literature. Basic principles of electrical engineering
Principles of circuit theory. AC and DC current. Power and work.
Electromagnetism- basic quantities, magnetic properties, magnetic circuits. Electromagnetic induction phenomenon. Self and mutual inductance.
Electrical and mechanical energy transformation- basic principles and relations, applications.
R, L, C elements in AC circuits.
Resonance circuits, real power, reactive power, power factor correction, filters.
AC circuits. Three-phase voltage generation. Four-cable system. Wye and delta connections.
Transformers and chokes- construction, principles and work analysis.
Types of transformers and their applications, autotransformers and current transformers.
Induction motor- construction, principles of work.
Types of induction motor works, load characteristics.
Starting, braking, speed control. Application of induction motors.
Synchronous machines- construction, principles of work, applications.
DC machines- construction, principles of work.
Types of DC motors, load characteristics, starting, braking and speed control, applications.
Introduction, safety instructions.
Real power in AC three-phase systems.
Three-phase transformer measurement.
Squirrel-cage induction motor measurement.
Squirrel-cage induction motor supplied with frequency converter.
DC shunt motor measurement.
DC series motor measurement.
Grades.
teaching_methods: traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
assessment_rules: For lectures, the final grade (P) is equal to the formative assessment (F1), which is based on a writing test. For laboratories, the final grade (P) is equal to the formative assessment (F1), which is based on laboratory reports.
